introduction_raw: This guide provides the steps needed to disassemble the washing machine so that you can open the water drain pump.
introduction_rendered: This guide provides the steps needed to disassemble the washing machine so that you can open the water drain pump.

lines.text_raw: '''UNPLUG POWER CORD; TURN OFF WATER SUPPLY.'''
lines.text_rendered: UNPLUG POWER CORD; TURN OFF WATER SUPPLY.

lines.text_raw: Check machine details on the inside of the main door.
lines.text_rendered: Check machine details on the inside of the main door.

lines.text_raw: Move washing machine away from wall to make rear and front accessible.
lines.text_rendered: Move washing machine away from wall to make rear and front accessible.

lines.text_raw: Using Torx T20, unscrew two screws (top left and top right on rear side) .
lines.text_rendered: Using Torx T20, unscrew two screws (top left and top right on rear side) .

lines.text_raw: Slide top backwards, lift it off, and put it aside.
lines.text_rendered: Slide top backwards, lift it off, and put it aside.

comments.title: Washing Machine Disassembly to Access Water Drain Pump
comments.text_raw: If you don’t mind a little bending and if you don’t need to remove the pump, then you can save time by skipping some steps. Skip steps 2 through 7, follow step 8, and in step 9 only remove the bottom two screws of the front panel, but don’t bother about the two hidden screws that hold the front panel at the top. After removing the bottom screws, you can lift the front panel at the bottom forward. This is easier if you tilt the machine backwards. There is then just enough room to undo the drain hose clamp and clean the pump from that side.
comments.text_rendered: If you don’t mind a little bending and if you don’t need to remove the pump, then you can save time by skipping some steps. Skip steps 2 through 7, follow step 8, and in step 9 only remove the bottom two screws of the front panel, but don’t bother about the two hidden screws that hold the front panel at the top. After removing the bottom screws, you can lift the front panel at the bottom forward. This is easier if you tilt the machine backwards. There is then just enough room to undo the drain hose clamp and clean the pump from that side.

steps.title: Remove detergent dispensing tray, and 3 screws

lines.text_raw: Push down blue part in the middle to release the tray, and pull it out completely.
lines.text_rendered: Push down blue part in the middle to release the tray, and pull it out completely.

lines.text_raw: Unscrew three T20 screws; the one on the lower right is shorter.
lines.text_rendered: Unscrew three T20 screws; the one on the lower right is shorter.

lines.text_raw: Unhook three hooks at the top (two shown).
lines.text_rendered: Unhook three hooks at the top (two shown).

lines.text_raw: On the inside, on the right, there is another hook (marked), sitting between two guiding notches without hooks.
lines.text_rendered: On the inside, on the right, there is another hook (marked), sitting between two guiding notches without hooks.

lines.text_raw: Release the cables by gently pressing the hooked guides. Note that the black part (marked by a rectangle) must be unlocked.
lines.text_rendered: Release the cables by gently pressing the hooked guides. Note that the black part (marked by a rectangle) must be unlocked.

lines.text_raw: Finally, unlock the connector (e.g. with your nails or a flat-blade screwdriver) and pull it out.
lines.text_rendered: Finally, unlock the connector (e.g. with your nails or a flat-blade screwdriver) and pull it out.

lines.text_raw: Put the control panel aside.
lines.text_rendered: Put the control panel aside.

comments.title: Washing Machine Disassembly to Access Water Drain Pump
comments.text_raw: The connector is held in place with a notched tab underneath. Press this tab down before attempting to disconnect the cable.
comments.text_rendered: The connector is held in place with a notched tab underneath. Press this tab down before attempting to disconnect the cable.

lines.text_raw: The drum is freely suspended. Wedge a towel on the rear side behind the drum to immobilize it. This will prevent damage when tilting the washing machine later on.
lines.text_rendered: The drum is freely suspended. Wedge a towel on the rear side behind the drum to immobilize it. This will prevent damage when tilting the washing machine later on.

lines.text_raw: ***DO NOT FORGET TO REMOVE THIS when reassembling!***
lines.text_rendered: DO NOT FORGET TO REMOVE THIS when reassembling!

comments.title: Washing Machine Disassembly to Access Water Drain Pump
comments.text_raw: Let the towel stick out over the backplane. That way you won’t forget it.
comments.text_rendered: Let the towel stick out over the backplane. That way you won’t forget it.

steps.title: Detach door seal from front cover

lines.text_raw: The rubber door seal is attached to the front cover by a metal wire and a spring.
lines.text_rendered: The rubber door seal is attached to the front cover by a metal wire and a spring.

lines.text_raw: Pry out the spring and pull away the wire.
lines.text_rendered: Pry out the spring and pull away the wire.

lines.text_raw: Unpeel the seal all the way round, and tuck it inside.
lines.text_rendered: Unpeel the seal all the way round, and tuck it inside.

comments.title: Washing Machine Disassembly to Access Water Drain Pump
comments.text_raw:
Excellent guide, very helpful, Thank you.

I’m just going to add that re-ritting the inner retaining ring can be a little tricky as the spring is very strong. I finally did it by first setting  the wire ring in place at the bottom, the left and the right; the ring was then short at the top; so, still pressing my thumb against the spring on the left (to stop it popping out of place) I used a screwdriver to lever the wire into place at the top right; then I slid the screwdriver around the seal, towards my thumb holding the spring on the left (this forced the wire ring into place without allowing it to pop out elsewhere).
comments.text_rendered:

steps.title: Remove drain/filter door, drain water, and unscrew

lines.text_raw: The round door (front bottom right) for the drain tube and filter can be removed, by opening it completely, and gently pulling out the left side of the hinge.
lines.text_rendered: The round door (front bottom right) for the drain tube and filter can be removed, by opening it completely, and gently pulling out the left side of the hinge.

lines.text_raw: '''DRAIN ANY REMAINING WATER'''.
lines.text_rendered: DRAIN ANY REMAINING WATER.

lines.text_raw: Unscrew two T20 screws.
lines.text_rendered: Unscrew two T20 screws.

lines.text_raw: Unscrew two (T20) screws at the top.
lines.text_rendered: Unscrew two (T20) screws at the top.

lines.text_raw: Tilt the whole washing machine towards its rear side to expose the front bottom. Lean it against a wall.
lines.text_rendered: Tilt the whole washing machine towards its rear side to expose the front bottom. Lean it against a wall.

lines.text_raw: Unscrew two (6mm hex-head) screws on the bottom.
lines.text_rendered: Unscrew two (6mm hex-head) screws on the bottom.

lines.text_raw: The front cover is held in place by plastic hooked pins. Slightly lift the front cover to unhook it.
lines.text_rendered: The front cover is held in place by plastic hooked pins. Slightly lift the front cover to unhook it.

lines.text_raw: On the inside, unclip something, and pull out a connector (for the door lock). The plastic emergency door release comes out easily. The image shows this when clip and connector are already disconnected.
lines.text_rendered: On the inside, unclip something, and pull out a connector (for the door lock). The plastic emergency door release comes out easily. The image shows this when clip and connector are already disconnected.

lines.text_raw: '''DO NOT FORGET TO PUT ALL THIS BACK on reassembly!'''
lines.text_rendered: DO NOT FORGET TO PUT ALL THIS BACK on reassembly!

comments.title: Washing Machine Disassembly to Access Water Drain Pump
comments.text_raw: REMINDER: Restore THREE things! Emergency release cable, door lock connector, and some unidentified attachment (the finger points there).
comments.text_rendered: REMINDER: Restore THREE things! Emergency release cable, door lock connector, and some unidentified attachment (the finger points there).

comments.title: Washing Machine Disassembly to Access Water Drain Pump
comments.text_raw: You can most easily access that unidenfied attachment through the door opening, by pushing back the rubber seal on that side. The connector however is hidden behind a plastic plate, and needs to be accessed from the outside at the right. Maybe undoing the attachment allows you to bend back that cover enough to access the connector through the door opening. (I didn’t try that yet).

lines.text_raw: Remove the plastic strip that protects the bottom edge.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the plastic strip that protects the bottom edge.

lines.text_raw: Unhook on the back, and tilt it forwards.
lines.text_rendered: Unhook on the back, and tilt it forwards.

lines.text_raw: Note the guiding notches to help you put it back.
lines.text_rendered: Note the guiding notches to help you put it back.

comments.title: Washing Machine Disassembly to Access Water Drain Pump
comments.text_raw: If you take care, you can leave this part in place.
comments.text_rendered: If you take care, you can leave this part in place.

lines.text_raw: Unscrew one (T20) screw.
lines.text_rendered: Unscrew one (T20) screw.

lines.text_raw: Tilt the plate back, and lift it. There is a hooked tab, and a guiding pin to help you reassemble the plate.
lines.text_rendered: Tilt the plate back, and lift it. There is a hooked tab, and a guiding pin to help you reassemble the plate.

lines.text_raw: Pull out the drain tube.
lines.text_rendered: Pull out the drain tube.

lines.text_raw: Put the cover plate aside.
lines.text_rendered: Put the cover plate aside.

lines.text_raw: Pull the power connector from the pump.
lines.text_rendered: Pull the power connector from the pump.

lines.text_raw: Using pliers, loosen the clamp on the hose from the tumbler and slide it back.
lines.text_rendered: Using pliers, loosen the clamp on the hose from the tumbler and slide it back.

lines.text_raw: Remove the hose.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the hose.

lines.text_raw: BE PREPARED FOR SOME WATER (use a towel or bowl).
lines.text_rendered: BE PREPARED FOR SOME WATER (use a towel or bowl).

comments.title: Washing Machine Disassembly to Access Water Drain Pump
comments.text_raw: Diconnecting the pump cable is only necessary when you want to take the pump out in its entirety.
comments.text_rendered: Diconnecting the pump cable is only necessary when you want to take the pump out in its entirety.

lines.text_raw: In my case, the pump inlet (where we just removed the hose coming from the tumbler) was clogged with debris and some cloth.
lines.text_rendered: In my case, the pump inlet (where we just removed the hose coming from the tumbler) was clogged with debris and some cloth.

lines.text_raw: This prevented draining, and even prevented removal of the filter. Thus, requiring disassembly. But we are not done yet.
lines.text_rendered: This prevented draining, and even prevented removal of the filter. Thus, requiring disassembly. But we are not done yet.

lines.text_raw: Unscrew four T20 screws.
lines.text_rendered: Unscrew four T20 screws.

lines.text_raw: Tilt the filter/pump unit (note the tab at the top), and pull it out from the back.
lines.text_rendered: Tilt the filter/pump unit (note the tab at the top), and pull it out from the back.

comments.title: Washing Machine Disassembly to Access Water Drain Pump
comments.text_raw: Only do this if you need to take out the pump (because otherwise you cannot clean it, or if you want to replace it).
comments.text_rendered: Only do this if you need to take out the pump (because otherwise you cannot clean it, or if you want to replace it).

replies.title: Washing Machine Disassembly to Access Water Drain Pump

lines.text_raw: At his point you can clean the water inlet, the filter, and the pump. The impeller should move freely. The pump itself can also be removed to replace it (but I did not do that).
lines.text_rendered: At his point you can clean the water inlet, the filter, and the pump. The impeller should move freely. The pump itself can also be removed to replace it (but I did not do that).

lines.text_raw: In my case, a significant amount of cloth got stuck in the water inlet, including a necklace. In the filter, there were some hairpins, and inside the pump itself, a coin and a pendent. LESSON: CLEAN THE FILTER MORE OFTEN, while you can stil remove it without disassembling the machine.

comments.title: Washing Machine Disassembly to Access Water Drain Pump
comments.text_raw:
Great instruction, worked with my Siemens WM16Y541NL/44 - it did take me more time though, about 2,5 hours taking everything apart and cleaning and the same putting the machine back together. I also cleaned the black inlet hose (that connects the drum to the pump), this had some more stuff in it like a coin. Also changed the pump. Getting the rubber back on was impossible for me by hand. After searching apparantly there are specialised pliers for this, which I would highly recommend. I ended up buying something in the hardware store, which i could use to keep the spring extended. And finally got the spring back on.

I don't understand why manufacturers make it so complex to get access to this pump. Why not have the bottom part of the door as a separate door you can open which gives access to the pump and filter directly, would save so much time and hassle.
